## THE CROWN — what "green" means for `rid-009` (Config/Data, but its failure mode is a boot halt)

**Why this section exists and is not folded into the ordinary per-story catalogue.** Every other
Config/Data story on this project ships a smoke-check-passes/smoke-check-fails verdict that, if
wrong, reddens a report. `rid-009` is different in kind, not degree: it is the **first story in
this project's history whose deliverable is shipped data consumed by a boot-time validation
pipeline that has never seen non-empty production content before.** Per F2 (verified in
`resource_item_database.gd::_load_definitions()`): today, `data_dir` missing → early-return
`success = true`, silently green. The moment `res://data/items/` exists with **any** entry,
`_check_tier0_family_coverage()` runs for the first time ever against real data. A malformed or
incomplete entry does not fail a test — **it halts the game itself at boot**, before any test
runner or manual QA session can even begin. Treat any red result from this story's own smoke
checks with S1 severity by default (game does not boot), not S2/S3 as a content bug would normally
warrant elsewhere.

### What GREEN means, defined precisely (three conjunctive conditions, all required)

1. **The tier-0 family coverage check passes.** `wood_block`, `stone_block`, `thatch_block` each
   register as the sole tier-0 `building_material` for their family; `_check_tier0_family_coverage()`
   raises no BLOCKING issue. Verified by Smoke-1 (tier-0 set) and Smoke-2 (category isolation) in
   the story's own QA Test Cases.
2. **Boot reaches `ACTIVE`.** Not "the validation function returns a green structured result in
   isolation" — the actual `GameWorld` boot sequence, run headlessly end-to-end with the shipped
   `res://data/items/` directory on disk, must reach `BootState.ACTIVE` with zero BLOCKING issues
   raised anywhere in the RID pipeline. This is Smoke-4 in the story's own QA Test Cases
   ("boot reaches Ready (green validation path)") — this plan requires it be read as **boot reaches
   ACTIVE**, the scene-world-management vocabulary, not merely "RID's own internal `Ready` state" —
   the two are related but not identical, and only the former is the player-observable claim.
3. **`is_need_functional(&"bed")` flips to TRUE in production** — against the real, Autoload-tier
   `ResourceItemDatabase` singleton (never a test-local mock config), because a real `bed.tres`
   with `category = furniture_fixture` and `id = &"bed"` is present in
   `need_functional_item_ids` (already defaulted) AND resolves via `ResourceItemDatabase.get_by_id`.
   This is the sprint's whole point (per the sprint file's own framing): *"one story flips a false
   branch to a true branch in three separate shipped, tested, green systems."*

**Sequencing gate carried from F2, restated as a QA requirement, not just an implementation
lever**: any intermediate commit in this story's own history must boot green. The three tier-0
materials MUST land in a commit that boots green on their own (satisfying condition 1) **before**
`bed.tres` is added. A lone `bed.tres` committed first is an expected-and-required-to-fail smoke
state, not a passing one — if a reviewer sees a red boot at an intermediate commit, check whether
tier-0 coverage was satisfied at that commit before treating it as a regression.

### The two pinned tests that MUST flip this sprint — named exactly, not paraphrased

Sprint 10's sign-off (§4.1, §4.4, condition #2) named this gap and pinned it into the suite as
**documented, deliberately-false assertions with their own class-doc explaining why**. Verified by
direct read (not by the sign-off's own summary) against the actual test files on disk. Three
functions across two files carry this pin:

1. **`neues-spiel/tests/unit/build_validation/shelter_classification_test.gd`**,
   `test_is_need_functional_unknown_id_returns_false_without_error` (lines 390–398): currently
   asserts `config.is_need_functional(&"bed") == false` — described in its own inline comment as
   proving only "the safe default, not the true branch (which needs real RID content story 008
   will supply)". **This is the exact BLOCKING DoD line inherited from Sprint 10 that was not met
   (sign-off §4.1, condition #2).**
2. **`neues-spiel/tests/unit/build_validation/warning_info_tiers_test.gd`**,
   `test_documented_limitation_bed_in_sealed_region_emits_zero_warning_pending_rid_content` (line
   511): currently asserts `bv.config.is_need_functional(&"bed") == false` and a sealed placed bed
   emits **zero** `sealed_space_warning`.
3. **`neues-spiel/tests/unit/build_validation/warning_info_tiers_test.gd`**,
   `test_documented_limitation_bed_unsheltered_open_emits_zero_info_pending_rid_content` (line 531):
   same pin, for `unsheltered_furniture_info` emitting zero.

The file's own class-doc (lines 1–38) is explicit that these two `warning_info_tiers_test.gd`
functions are "**PINNED as a documented, named limitation... and must be revisited (flipped to
expect real emissions) the day RID content for 'bed' ships**" — this sprint is that day.

**Binding requirement, added by this plan**: all three functions above must be rewritten this
sprint into **genuine two-branch tests** — the false/zero branch retained for an unknown or
non-functional id (still a real, useful assertion), and a new TRUE/non-zero branch asserted against
the real, now-authored `&"bed"` id. A test suite that simply deletes these three functions without
replacing them with a passing true-branch equivalent does not satisfy this requirement — the
false-branch coverage for unknown ids must not be lost.

### The flip must be DEMONSTRATED, not merely asserted

Consistent with this project's own established non-vacuity discipline (`scene-006`'s
`AC-PROBE-IS-NON-VACUOUS`, `presentation-003`'s call-site allowlist, `build-validation-002`'s
furniture-transparency proof-by-construction): a rewritten assertion that happens to pass is not
sufficient evidence on its own that a real flip occurred, because a test author could accidentally
write a true-branch assertion that would also pass against stale/mocked data.

**Binding requirement**: the commit body (or a dedicated
`production/qa/evidence/rid-009-bed-functional-flip-evidence.md`) must record, for each of the
three functions above:
- The exact pre-sprint assertion (quoted, as pinned in Sprint 10 — already quoted above).
- The exact post-sprint assertion (quoted).
- Confirmation that the true-branch run was executed **against the real `ResourceItemDatabase`
  Autoload with `res://data/items/bed.tres` actually present on disk** — not a test-local
  `MockResourceItemDatabase` standing in for it. (A test-local double is fine for other unit tests
  in this suite; it is specifically not fine as the proof for THIS claim, because the entire point
  is that production data now resolves the id.)
- The suite counts before/after this story's commit (mirroring `scene-006`'s and `needs-mood-006`'s
  own precedent of recording exact before/after test-case counts in the commit body).

This is this plan's own addition (Content Requirement, per `/qa-plan` protocol) — none of `rid-009`,
`build-validation-006`, or `build-validation-008`'s own story files require the flip be
*demonstrated* this precisely; they only require it be *true*. Given that Sprint 10 shipped this
exact gap silently once already (green-looking suite, false claim buried in a docstring), demanding
demonstration rather than bare assertion is the correction.

## `scene-007`'s anti-vacuity assertion (Gate G2 pre-specification, the fourth ship-green-and-uncalled)

**Why this is defined here, before the story file exists.** `scene-007` does not yet have a story
file (Gate G2). This plan pre-specifies the one requirement that must not be lost in authoring, so
that `/story-readiness` has a concrete QA bar to check against rather than discovering the gap
after the fact — the same discipline `presentation-003`'s S10 gate used, minus a TD spec to
transcribe (this sprint has none; the scope derives only from building-ui KC3 + ADR-0005).

**The failure mode this guards against (S06's own lesson, restated in the sprint file)**: a test
that asserts the PRESENCE of a call (`Valley.get_injected_tier_modules()` lists the tool nodes;
`GameWorld.setup()` was invoked; a node exists at a given path) can pass vacuously — it proves
wiring exists, not that the wiring does anything a player's action could reach. `scene-006`'s own
non-vacuity proof is the template: its obvious/vacuous assertion form
(`get_need_value(...) == 100.0`) was kept in the test file **only as a documented, explicitly-
labeled contrast**, never as the actual proof; the actual proof drove a real tick through the real
production tick source and asserted an **observable consequence** that is impossible unless the
production wiring is real.

### The assertion `scene-007` must contain (binding on the story's own Test Evidence section)

1. **Not this** (rejected form, name it explicitly in the story file as a documented non-proof,
   exactly as `scene-006` did): asserting that `Valley.get_injected_tier_modules()` includes
   `BuildEditorMode`/`WallTool`/etc., or that `BuildProjectRegistry`/`ConstructionJobQueue` are
   non-null after boot. These prove construction, not reachability — a regression that constructs
   the objects but never routes an actual placement/demolition intent through them would still pass
   this form.
2. **This** (the required proof): drive a placement or demolition **intent** through the actually
   **hosted** tool chain — e.g., a `BlockTool` (or `FurnitureTool`, given this sprint's crown)
   reached via its scene-hosted path receives a simulated commit intent, and the assertion observes
   the **consequence** at the far end of the chain: either a `VoxelWorldGrid` cell state change (for
   an instant/legal case) or a `ConstructionJobQueue`/`BuildProjectRegistry` entry created (for a
   job-based case) — something a save-load, a UI panel, or a human player could independently
   observe, not an internal call-count on a mock.
3. **The deletion probe, mandatory, mirroring `scene-006`'s own recorded methodology exactly**: once
   during development, comment out (or otherwise disable) the hosting call this story adds — the
   line(s) that attach `BuildEditorMode`/the four tools/`FurnitureTool`/`GhostPreview`/
   `UndoRedoStack`/`BuildProjectRegistry`/`ConstructionJobQueue` to the scene or hand them to
   `ConstructionTickLoop` — re-run the assertion from point 2 above **in isolation**, and record the
   **observed failure** (exact test-runner output: failure count, which assertion failed, exit
   code) in the commit body. Then restore the hosting call verbatim (`git diff` against the
   restored file should show a clean, comment-free restore, exactly as `scene-006`'s commit body
   records) and re-run green. **A story that skips this step does not satisfy this plan's gate**,
   regardless of how the rest of its test suite reads.
4. **If the "host tool tier only" fallback lever is pulled** (sprint file's own named lever: defer
   `BuildProjectRegistry`/`ConstructionJobQueue`/`UndoRedoStack` hosting to S12 if full scope proves
   too large), the deletion probe above is required for **whichever hosting the story actually
   ships** — the assertion narrows with the scope, but the discipline does not relax. Record which
   scope was shipped, explicitly, in the same evidence.

**This plan requires `/story-readiness`, once `scene-007`'s file is authored, to confirm the story's
own Test Evidence section commits to points 1–4 above before the gate closes** — not merely
"an integration test exists."

## The demolition chain's owed debt — `building-017`'s non-vacuous re-verification of `needs-mood-010`'s revocation claim

**The debt, named precisely (D8 option (c), Sprint 10 sign-off, `building-017`'s own story file).**
`needs-mood-010`'s crown (Sprint 10) proved bed-revocation by directly firing
`FurnitureBedProvider.furniture_revoked` from the test's own Act phase — a real signal, but never
fired by a real demolition job, because no demolition system existed yet. `building-017`'s own
story file names this explicitly: *"this story owes its non-vacuous re-verification — re-run
`shelter_recovery_live_pair_test.gd`'s revocation case driven by a real demolition job
completing."*

### The follow-on assertion, defined precisely

Once `building-017` lands (and its own dependencies `building-009`/`building-015` are in place),
**the SAME `shelter_recovery_live_pair_test.gd` revocation scenario** (not a new, separate test
file — extending the existing crown test, per this project's established pattern of extending
rather than duplicating boot/integration harnesses) must be re-run with:

1. **Setup unchanged from the crown**: a real `NeedsMood`, a real `VillagerAi`, a real
   `FurnitureRegistry.place()`-laid 1×2 bed, a real `BuildValidation` classifying it sheltered, a
   real villager Recovering in it (via `start_recovery`).
2. **The trigger changed to the real path**: instead of calling
   `FurnitureBedProvider.furniture_revoked.emit(...)` directly, drive an actual `building-017`
   demolition order against the Built bed to completion — i.e., create the demolition order (via
   the removal tool or a direct call into `building-009`'s job contract, per `building-017`'s own
   AC17), feed it `base_demolition_ticks[furniture]` worth of on-site tick events through the real
   tick mechanism (mirroring `building-009`'s own AC66 mocked-claim pattern), and let the job
   complete.
3. **Assert the SAME three consequences the crown already proves, now via the real trigger**:
   - The villager wakes / is interrupted out of Recovering (the crown's own existing assertion,
     re-pointed at the new trigger).
   - `stop_recovery` credits **zero** for that tick (no partial credit at the interruption instant —
     the crown's existing zero-credit assertion).
   - Ownership/occupancy dissolves — the villager no longer holds a claim on the now-demolished
     bed.
4. **Assert the revocation-event TIMING contract from `building-017`'s own AC17/Implementation
   Notes**: the furniture-revocation event fires on demolition-order **completion**, not at order
   creation — assert zero revocation-consequence at the instant the order is created (the bed keeps
   functioning normally, matching AC17's "not blocked by usage... not removed until completion"),
   and all three consequences above land only at completion. This mirrors `build-validation-005`'s
   own T0/T1 connected-scenario discipline from Sprint 9 (both halves proven in ONE run, not two
   independently-passable tests) — apply the same shape here: one connected scenario asserting
   "nothing at creation" AND "everything at completion," not two separate tests that could each
   pass while their conjunction is false.

### PASS bar

All four points above proven inside one connected scenario in
`shelter_recovery_live_pair_test.gd` (or its direct extension). **This is the concrete bar for "the
debt is paid"** — the sprint's own DoD line ("re-verifies against a REAL demolition job... BLOCKING;
this is D8 option (c)'s owed follow-on AC and the reason the crown was allowed to ship in S10") is
satisfied only when this exact scenario passes, not when `building-017`'s own isolated unit suite
passes on its own fixtures.

### Cross-lane serialization note (carried forward, S10 §5 lesson, applied literally here)

`shelter_recovery_live_pair_test.gd` is the `ai-programmer` (lane B) file, but `building-017` is a
`godot-specialist` (lane C) story. **Serialize this specific re-run against anything lane B has
open** — if `villager-ai-019`/`presentation-001` Sub-B are mid-edit in the same working tree when
`building-017`'s re-verification is attempted, a red result must be re-run in isolation (clean
stash / separate branch) before it is read as a real regression, per the exact process lesson the
Sprint 10 sign-off recorded (§5): *"a suite run is only evidence about the change under test if
nothing else in the tree is mid-edit."* Lane C is five stories deep in one tree this sprint — this
is the single most likely sprint yet for that failure mode to recur.

### building-031 — Removal tool base — Logic
**What to test**: AC41 a Planned blueprint cell removed directly (not via undo) → Canceled, ghost
removed, claimed job revoked; Queued/UnderConstruction cancel + graceful job revoke; a
floor-excavation cell restores `restore_value` on cancel (Story 012 coordination); a Built cell is
explicitly NOT handled here (routes to 015/009 — assert this boundary, do not silently let 031's
suite drift into covering 015's scope).
**Terminology flag (this plan's own finding, not in either story file)**: `building-031`'s AC41
names the target state "**Planned**"; `building-015`'s AC73/AC74 name the same class of not-yet-
Built cell "**Draft**" and "**Queued/UnderConstruction**." Confirm at implementation time that
"Planned" (031) and "Draft" (015) denote the SAME micro-state under two names, not two different
states — if they are the same state, one test suite risks either duplicating the other's coverage
or, worse, each assuming the other covers a case neither actually does. Flagged for the
implementer/reviewer to resolve explicitly (naming only, not a scheduling blocker).
